title: ‘Lick your boots’: Anthony Albanese mocked in crude statue with Donald Trump outside Victorian parliament
text:

A crude statue of Anthony Albanese and Donald Trump has been removed after it was secretly installed in front of Victorian parliament in the Melbourne CBD.

The statue of the Prime Minister and US President was secretly installed on Gordon Reserve along Spring St about 7am on Friday.

The statue depicts Mr Albanese dressed in a Joy Division T-shirt on his knees in front of Mr Trump, who was donning a suit and baseball cap.

A water pump installed at Mr Trump’s waist appears to spray water at Mr Albanese’s chest and face.

An activist group has installed an explicit fountain statue outside Victorian parliament depicting Prime Minister Anthony Albanese kneeling before Donald Trump.

The installation was titled “A golden opportunity”, with a plaque underneath that read: “May I lick your boots, boss?”.

Online, activist group The New Radicals has claimed responsibility for the statue.

A City of Melbourne spokesman confirmed the statue had been dismantled and removed from the site by about 9.30am on Friday.

“On Friday morning, the City of Melbourne became aware of an unauthorised installation in Gordon Reserve,” he told NewsWire.

“Council officers immediately attended the scene to remove the installation.

“Council is also reviewing Safe City Camera footage and will provide relevant material to Victoria Police upon application.”

Police believe the statue was erected on its own improvised plinth in the parkland and are investigating whether there are “any criminal offences related to the incident”.

This is the latest art installation claimed by the activist group.

A parody amnesty bin was installed in front of Premier Jacinta Allan’s office in Bendigo in October last year. “Sh*t Premier Safe Disposal Bin” a plaque on the front of the bin read.

“Please remove from power before throwing in the bin.”

Months earlier, a large nose covered in brown sludge was installed out the front of Defence Minister Richard Marles’ office in Geelong.

“This memorial erected by The New Radicals in honour of Australia’s biggest brown-noser,” the plaque read.

Originally published as ‘Lick your boots’: Anthony Albanese mocked in crude statue with Donald Trump outside Victorian parliament
